chain.g: to exit, depart, go forth, come forth

ety.text: Old French issuebor. Middle English issue English issue From Middle English issue, from Old French issue (“an exit, a way out”), feminine past participle of issir (“to exit”), from Latin exeō (“go out, exit”), from prefix ex- (“out”) + eō (“go”). The legal meaning originated from the concept of "the end or result of pleadings in a suit (by presenting the point to be determined by trial)," leading to the sense of "the controversy over facts in a trial" (early 14th century, Anglo-French).

senses.d: A movement of soldiers towards an enemy, a sortie.
The outflow of a bodily fluid, particularly (now rare) in abnormal amounts.
ex: The technique minimizes the issue of blood from the incision.

senses.d: The bodily fluid drained through a natural or artificial issue.
ex: For she doted upon their paramours, whose flesh is as the flesh of asses, and whose issue is like the issue of horses.

senses.d: Offspring: one's natural child or children.
ex: He died intestate and without issue, so the extended family have all lawyered up.
Although his own kingdom disappeared, his issue went on to rule a quarter of Europe.

senses.d: A race of people considered as the descendants of some common ancestor.
The produce or income derived from farmland or rental properties.
ex: 3. A conveys to B all right to the real property aforementioned for a term of _____ years, with all said real property's attendant issues, rents, and profits.

senses.d: Income derived from fines levied by a court or law-enforcement officer; the fines themselves.
The entrails of a slaughtered animal.
Any action or deed performed by a person.
To flow out, to proceed from, to come out or from.
ex: The water issued forth from the spring.
The rents issuing from the land permitted him to live as a man of independent means.

senses.d: To rush out, to sally forth.
ex: The men issued from the town and attacked the besiegers.

senses.d: To extend into, to open onto.
ex: The road issues into the highway.

senses.d: To turn out in a certain way, to result in.
ex: But, for Livy, Roman patriotism is overriding, and this issues, of course, in an antiquarian attention to the city's origins.

senses.d: To end up as, to turn out being, to become as a result.
ex:
And let his foes like flockes of feareful Roes,
Purſude by hunters, flie his angry lookes,
That I may ſee him iſſue Conquerour.

senses.d: To come to a point in fact or law on which the parties join issue.
To send out; to put into circulation.
ex: The Federal Reserve issues US dollars.
The prison issued new uniforms for the inmates.
The court issued a writ of mandamus.
